observation.description: The validator vocabulary is asymmetric across the three authoring positions and the field-side refusal does not name the supported spelling. v.array(...) is accepted in RESULT schemas (results.records nested arrays, A4 precedent) and in mutation ARGS (completeAnswer's citations array validated fine), but a TABLE FIELD declared v.array(v.number()) refuses at generation with SCHEMA_INVALID_VALIDATOR: 'sourceEmbeddings.vector has unsupported validator primitive/field type "array"/"Json"' — a message that names the internal Json primitive yet does not say that v.json() IS the documented, working column type for exactly this value (guide getting-started/your-first-backend.md lists it in the complete validator set). This arm first shipped a JSON-string workaround (vector and citations as JSON text with stringify/parse at every boundary) before a probe showed v.json() generates and round-trips arrays/objects natively. Cost: one avoidable modeling detour on a natural research-room shape (citations {sourceId,title}[], 32-dim embedding vectors).
evidence: demos/improvement-sweep/arms/a5-snapback-web/evidence/app/schema.mjs (final v.json() shape with the observation note)

competitorOutcome.description: Convex table fields take v.array(v.number()) and nested objects directly, so the same schema spelling works in every position; frozen 0102 research-room arms stored embedding fixtures as ordinary array columns without a detour.
competitorOutcome.reference: diaries/0031-research-room-backend-bakeoff.diary.md (Convex arm: one schema declared ordinary, full-text, and vector indexes)

mustNotRegress: results.records/args accepting structured v.array validators, and v.json() fields round-tripping arrays and nested objects through insert, patch, live queries, and versioned seeds (all proven this arm).
smallestCoherentFix: Either accept v.array(inner) on table fields as sugar for v.json() (keeping the stored primitive identical), or make the SCHEMA_INVALID_VALIDATOR diagnostic say 'use v.json() for structured columns' — plus one guide line in your-first-backend.md noting that arrays as column values are spelled v.json().
acceptanceWitness: A clean consumer declaring a v.array field either generates successfully (sugar) or receives a diagnostic that names v.json(); a grep of the diagnostic text for 'v.json' passes.
